newsitem.title: USA: Magician Copperfield sues Paris Match for defamation.
newsitem.headline: Magician Copperfield sues Paris Match for defamation.

text.p: Magician David Copperfield launched what could be his greatest trick on Wednesday -- prying $30 million damages from Paris Match magazine for alleging his romance with supermodel Claudia Schiffer was a sham.
"That claim is absolutely false in every respect," said his defamation suit filed in Los Angeles Superior Court against the French magazine's publishers and a rival magician, Herbert Becker.
It said Paris Match -- "a sensationalist photo magazine" -- had spread around the world the false story that Copperfield and the German-born Schiffer had taken part in a fraud.
The story said the couple pretended to be romantically involved, but that Schiffer was actually being paid by Copperfield to accompany him and pretend to be his fiancee.
The magazine said the "contract" was for publicity's sake.
It said Schiffer pretended to be Copperfield's "girlfriend, fiancee and confidante" for a regular fee and that she was forbidden to have a romantic relationship "with any other man or woman."

Paris Match said Schiffer did not even like the New Jersey-born magician and that their romance was a scheme planned by Schiffer's mother. It alleged Copperfield was unknown in Germany in 1993 and entered into the relationship to build up his fame among audiences there.
In his suit, Copperfield, who was described as "a well-known illusionist," said "there is no such contract and never has been."
"Mr. Copperfield and Ms. Schiffer met on the job, fell in love and plan to marry. They are not pretending to be anything to anyone," the suit said.
It said the magazine called attention to its "grotesquely false story" with the headline: "David and Claudia - A Love Under Contract."

The false story had been circulated and the "vicious libel" repeated by other media around the world and on the Internet, damaging both Copperfield and his German fiancee personally and professionally, according to the suit.
Copperfield said he would give any damages to charity and also that Schiffer planned to file her own action elsewhere.
In addition to the $30 million in compensatory damages he is seeking, Copperfield asked for punitive damages against Becker, who his suit described as "a spiteful and vindictive former magician."
The suit said Paris Match's story was based on fake documents provided by Becker, "who is monstrously envious of plaintiff's success" and conducted an "obsessive vendetta" against Copperfield.
